# Descent through extensions of fields generated by conjugates

<a id="statement"></a>
## Short multiplicative relations required for descent

Let \(x\) be a nontorsion reciprocal algebraic unit of degree \(d\), and put \(m=L_x=d h(x)\), where \(L_z\) denotes the logarithmic Mahler measure of the primitive minimal polynomial of \(z\).
Assume distinct conjugates of \(x\) have nontorsion quotient.
Choose one representative of each pair of inverse conjugates, calling the pair its label.
All ranks and spans of algebraic numbers below refer to their classes in \((\overline{\mathbb Q}^{\times}/\mu)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q\), where \(\mu\) denotes the roots of unity.
A circuit is a minimally dependent set of distinct labels.
Neither dependence nor the represented span depends on the choices of orientations.

Fix \(r\ge1\) and \(M>0\), and assume \(m\le M\).
For \(j\ge1\) set \(A_j=j((j+1)((j+1)!)^j-j)\).
Let \(F\) be generated by any collection of conjugates of rank at most \(r\), and let \(n=[F(y):F]\) for a nonzero algebraic number \(y\).
There is \(c_{r,M}>0\) such that for all sufficiently large \(d\), if
\[
               n\le c_{r,M}\frac{d}{(\log(3d))^{A_{r+1}}},             \tag{1}
\]
then the following exclusions hold.

* If \(m\) is minimal among all positive logarithmic Mahler measures of algebraic numbers of degree at most \(d\), a strict descent \(0<L_y<m\) requires a circuit of size from \(3\) to \(2r\) among the original labels.
  It also requires \(\gg_{r,M} d/(\log(3d))^{2A_r}\) strictly exterior conjugates of \(x\), regardless of multiplicative relations.
  In particular for \(r=1\) there is no such descent, of any exterior signature.
* If \(x\) is a Salem number and \(m\) is minimal just among the positive measures of Salem numbers of degree at most \(d\), there is no strict descent to another Salem number through (1).
  The output and input fields may initially be different.
* More generally, without any degree minimum, \(h(y)\le m/d\) and (1) force the class of \(y\) into the span of the selected conjugates.
  For each nontorsion such \(y\), take a minimal independent support of size \(s\le r\) from the selection.
  At \(s=1\), \(L_y\) is attained by a unit of degree \(d\) in a conjugate field of \(x\).
  At \(s\ge2\), if the labels have no circuit of size at most \(2s\), then
  \[
                 L_y\gg_s \frac{(d/m)^{s-1}}{(\log(3d))^{A_s}}.       \tag{2}
  \]
  Once \(y\) is known to lie in the multiplicative span modulo torsion, these last two conclusions hold in arbitrary extensions, without (1) or a height assumption.

Thus the degree restriction is on an extension over the field jointly generated by the source conjugates.
It need not bound the degree of a formula for \(y\) or the degree of \(y\) over \(\mathbb Q\).
The [single-field result at degree minima](Yin_C_G0345_v78.md#minimum) also identifies small values in the original field.
The [Salem monomial-radical results](Yin_C_G0866_v1.md#external-radical-degree) concern values already known to have a monomial power and include finer degree information for that domain.
The estimates below also quantify the number of distinct supports needed if a small radical has a circuit.

<a id="fields"></a>
## Field closure of a bounded-rank collection

Choose a basis \(u_1,\ldots,u_j\) from a collection of original conjugates and put \(F_0=\mathbb Q(u_1,\ldots,u_j)\).
For any conjugate \(v\) in their span there are \(q>0\), integers \(b_i\) and \(\zeta\in\mu\) with \(v^q=\zeta\prod_i u_i^{b_i}\).
An automorphism of \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\) fixing \(F_0\) sends \(v\) to a conjugate whose quotient by \(v\) is torsion.
The hypothesis on conjugates makes this quotient one, so \(v\in F_0\).
Thus the field of the whole collection equals \(F_0\) and has degree at most \(d^j\).
The rank-zero collection is empty and its field is \(\mathbb Q\).
Any dependent pair of distinct labels would satisfy \(u^b v^c\in\mu\) with \(bc\ne0\).
Equality of the positive heights of \(u,v\) forces \(|b|=|c|\), making \(u/v\) or \(u/v^{-1}\) torsion and contradicting the distinct labels.

For \(j\) independent nonzero numbers the [Amoroso–David height product theorem](../audits/literature/AD99/Yin_U001.md#ad99-u001) gives
\[
              \prod_{\ell=1}^j h(v_\ell)
                         \ge\frac{c_j}{D(\log(3D))^{A_j}},
   \qquad D=[\mathbb Q(v_1,\ldots,v_j):\mathbb Q].
\]
One can increase \(D\) on the right.
If \(y\) is independent of the \(j\)-element basis and \(h(y)\le m/d\), apply the theorem at rank \(j+1\) and joint degree at most \(nd^j\).
It gives the necessary inequality
\[
             n m^{j+1}(\log(3nd^j))^{A_{j+1}}\ge c_{j+1}d .          \tag{3}
\]
For \(0\le j\le r\), \(n\le d\) and \(m\le M\), the logarithm is at most \((r+1)\log(3d)\) and the exponents are nondecreasing.
Taking the constant in (1) smaller than the resulting finite minimum contradicts (3), proving the assertion about the span, including \(j=0\).
In particular, for large \(d\) at bounded \(m\) the conjugates in \(\mathbb Q(u_1,\ldots,u_j)\) are exactly the original conjugates in their multiplicative span for \(j\le r\).
For a conjugate outside the span its relative degree over this field satisfies (3) with \(n\le d\).

<a id="norm"></a>
## External radicals and the number of supports over their value

Suppose \(y^q=\zeta\prod_{i=1}^s u_i^{b_i}\) for an independent choice of \(s\ge1\) labels, \(b_i\ne0\), \(q>0\) and \(\zeta\in\mu\).
Then \(y\) is a unit, since \(y\) and \(y^{-1}\) are integral over the algebraic integers.
Let \(U=\mathbb Q(u_1,\ldots,u_s)\), \(K=U(y)\), \(Y=\mathbb Q(y)\), \(p=[K:Y]\) and \(e=[K:U]\).
All images of \(y\) over \(U\) differ from it by torsion factors, since their \(q\)-th powers do.
Consequently \(w=N_{K/U}y\) is a torsion multiple of \(y^e\) and \(h(w)=e h(y)\).
In particular
\[
                            [U:\mathbb Q] h(w)=p L_y .                \tag{4}
\]
The class of \(w\) has nonzero coefficients on each of the \(s\) independent labels.
Replacing \(u_s\) by \(w\) therefore leaves an independent \(s\)-tuple in \(U\).
Its height product is \((m/d)^{s-1}h(w)\).
The height product theorem with degree at most \([U:\mathbb Q]\le d^s\) and (4) give
\[
                     p L_y\gg_s \frac{(d/m)^{s-1}}
                                              {(\log(3d))^{A_s}} .    \tag{5}
\]
No exponent, torsion order or degree of the external radical occurs in this estimate.

The number \(p\) counts the possible ordered tuples of images of \((u_1,\ldots,u_s)\) over \(Y\), since \(K\) is generated by this tuple over \(Y\).
Each image gives a representation of the same class of \(y\).
If its support differs from the original, subtracting the two rational representations gives a nontrivial dependence on their union of at most \(2s\) distinct labels.
The coefficients on labels in their symmetric difference are nonzero.
In the absence of such a circuit, all image tuples therefore have the same underlying label set and \(p\le2^s s!\).
This proves (2).

For \(s=1\), fixing \(y\) sends its support conjugate \(u\) to a torsion multiple, hence fixes \(u\).
Thus \(U\subseteq Y\) and \(p=1\).
Fixing \(w\) also fixes \(u\) by the same calculation, since \(w\) is a torsion multiple of \(y^e\).
As \(w\in U\), it generates \(U\).
Equation (4) now gives \(L_w=L_y\) for this nontorsion unit of degree \(d\).

<a id="records"></a>
## Degree minima and the Salem specialization

At a minimum among all positive measures through degree \(d\), \(0<L_y<m\) requires \([Y:\mathbb Q]>d\), so \(h(y)<m/d\).
Under (1) apply the span result and take a support from a basis, omitting coordinates of weight zero.
Support zero would give torsion, and the one-label norm would contradict the same minimum.
For \(2\le s\le r\) at bounded \(m\), the bound (2) eventually exceeds \(M\), uniformly over the finitely many \(s\).
Thus a circuit on at most \(2r\) labels is necessary.
If a degree minimum is taken among all positive integer-polynomial measures, the same comparison with a minimal polynomial applies.
When the least degree attaining that minimum is used, the torsion-compression hypothesis follows from the [all-power norm descent](Yin_C_G0231_v1.md#all-positive-power-existence-descent), since a torsion quotient makes conjugate powers coincide at some exponent.

For a Salem input every set of distinct inverse labels is independent modulo torsion.
Indeed send any specified label to the pair formed by the Salem number and its inverse.
All other labels then have modulus one, so taking the modulus of any relation forces the specified coefficient to vanish, as in the [Salem conjugate independence argument](Yin_C_G0165_v1.md#off-pair-salem-ratio-proof).
The same test excludes a torsion quotient of distinct conjugates, with the two members of one pair treated by nontorsion of the original number.
If both the competing output and \(x\) are Salem numbers, minimality just among Salem numbers again implies \(h(y)<m/d\) for a strict descent.
For two or more support labels (2) precludes this at large \(d\).
In the one-label case take the embedding in which \(y>1\).
The equation \(y^q=\zeta u^b\) forces \(u\) to be either the positive Salem number \(x\) or \(x^{-1}\) after identifying the unique positive exterior conjugate with \(x\).
Positivity on both sides forces \(\zeta=1\).
Every positive power of a Salem number retains its field, since two conjugates with the same power would have torsion quotient.
The same holds for a negative nonzero exponent by inversion.
The equality of powers therefore gives \(\mathbb Q(y)=\mathbb Q(x)\) in this embedding, contradicting the strict Salem degree minimum.

<a id="multiplicity"></a>
## How many disjoint supports a small radical requires

At fixed rank \(s\ge1\) and bounded \(m\), the full span of \(s\) independent conjugates contains at most \(O_{s,M}((\log(3d))^{A_s})\) original labels.
To see this, let \(\Gamma\) be the free abelian group generated by those conjugate classes that lie in the span, and let \(H=m/d\).
It is finitely generated and has rank \(s\), with representatives of all its classes in \(U\) by field closure.
Height on the group is unchanged by torsion, is homogeneous under integer multiplication, and satisfies the triangle inequality.
Only finitely many classes have height at most any fixed bound, by the fixed-field degree and elementary coefficient bounds for the unit representatives.
Starting with the zero space, choose a class of smallest height \(\lambda_j\) outside the rational span of the previous \(j-1\) choices.
Then \(0<\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_s\le H\), and the product theorem gives \(\prod\lambda_j\gg_s [U:\mathbb Q]^{-1}(\log(3d))^{-A_s}\).
Choose a lattice basis adapted to these nested rational spans, possible since their intersections with \(\Gamma\) are saturated subgroups and the successive quotients are free of rank one.
In coordinate \(j\) reduce modulo the smallest power of two \(N_j>2H/\lambda_j\).
These moduli are nonincreasing and \(N_j\le4H/\lambda_j\).
If two distinct classes of height at most \(H\) have the same residues, let \(j\) be their last differing coordinate.
Dividing the difference by \(N_j\) gives an element of \(\Gamma\) outside the preceding span, as \(N_j\) divides all earlier moduli.
Its height is at most \(2H/N_j<\lambda_j\), a contradiction.
The number of such classes is at most \((4H)^s/\prod\lambda_j\ll_s m^s(\log(3d))^{A_s}\).
Representatives of distinct original labels are distinct modulo torsion, proving the count.

The same count bounds the denominators in the span conclusion.
Let \(E\) contain \(U\) with \([E:U]=n_0\), let \(\Lambda\) be generated by the \(s\) independent support classes, and let \(\widetilde\Lambda\) consist of the classes in \(E^\times/\mu(E)\) whose nonzero integer multiples belong to \(\Lambda\).
Each coset modulo \(\Lambda\) has a representative with rational coordinates of absolute value at most \(1/2\) in the support basis, by subtracting integer coordinates.
Its height is at most \(sH/2\) by clearing denominators and using subadditivity, and every representative is a unit.
Fixed-degree finiteness thus makes the index finite, so \(\widetilde\Lambda\) is a free abelian group of rank \(s\).
Repeat the preceding residue count on this group at radius \(sH\), now using the height product bound at degree at most \([E:\mathbb Q]\le n_0d^s\).
The successive minima are still at most \(H\) because the original basis is independent.
This gives
\[
     [\widetilde\Lambda:\Lambda]\ll_s
             n_0m^s(\log(3n_0d^s))^{A_s}.
\]
For a class of height at most \(H\) in this saturation, take the index as a common denominator for its coordinates.
The absolute numerator of each nonzero coordinate equals the index of the lattice obtained by replacing that basis conjugate by the given class, by the determinant formula in a basis of \(\widetilde\Lambda\).
The same index estimate applies there since all replacement heights are at most \(H\), and the surrounding field \(E\) is unchanged.

For a radical as in (5) with \(2\le s\le r\) and \(0<L_y\le M\), the \(p\) ordered tuples give at least \(p/(2^s s!)\gg_{s,M}d^{s-1}/(\log(3d))^{A_s}\) distinct supports.
For any specified label there are \(O_s(d^{s-2})\) choices of a further \(s-2\) labels on a support containing it.
If these \(s-1\) labels have a completion, their span together with the class of \(y\) is the rank-\(s\) span of that completion, since its missing label has a nonzero coefficient.
Every possible final label lies in that same span, giving at most \(O_{s,M}((\log(3d))^{A_s})\) completions by the count just proved.
Greedily taking a support and removing all those that meet it therefore leaves a family of pairwise disjoint supports of size
\[
                              \gg_{s,M}\frac{d}{(\log(3d))^{2A_s}} .
\]
Each represents the same class of \(y\).
Since \(y\) is a unit and \(L_y>0\), some embedding has \(|y|>1\) by the definition of its measure.
Extend that embedding to the algebraic closure and apply it to every representation.
The transformed supports remain pairwise disjoint, and every one must contain a label off the unit circle because its monomial has modulus different from one.
Each such inverse label supplies exactly one strictly exterior conjugate of \(x\).
This proves the asserted lower bound on their number whenever the strict descent has at least two support labels, using \(A_s\le A_r\).
Thus even allowing short circuits, an exterior count \(o(d/(\log(3d))^{2A_r})\) precludes the indicated descents at through-degree minima.
The case with both enough exterior conjugates and enough representations remains unresolved.
